timeline.body:
Introduce a new class `QueryTranslatorSpecTests` which uses a text file,
to read and assert translation of planned and optimised queries similar to
the approach already used in EQL.

Furthermore:
 - move the reading/parsing of that file to the common `ql`
module, to avoid repeating code between EQL & SQL.
 - rename test names to remove `_` and words like `Translate`,
or `Painless` which are superfluous.
 - rename EQL tests from `QueryFolderXXXTests` to
 `QueryTranslatorXXXTests`

Closes: #65417
"no assumptions"? maybe also "of a complete line"? or whatever you intended.
I suppose this comment (and the one below) is to be removed?
what's the `"null"` for? A NOP?

reply.body: This was for the EQL corresponding tests, Removing, you simply add a terminating `;` to have no assertions.

timeline.body: if a test's translation consists of `;` (or `null)` only, wouldn't this just add previous' test translation (i.e. matchers)?

reply.body: Sure, but `null` is removed now as a valid keyword to denote no matchers, and `;` is a disallowed keyword for the the matching string which works ok for us. I don't think we should complicate things more.

timeline.body:
These queries are checked only for validity not for translation correct?
If so it makes sense to move them to a different file, to indicate a different type of check.

reply.body: Sure, yep, all the subquery related are just checked that are correctly analysed planned and optimised.

For the EQL tests that currently reside in one file, I use only the test name as it was, i.e.: For the SQL tests I use a `/` to separate the filename from the test name, since we use similar approach for the YAML tests. i.e.: If you think that causes any trouble with running tests from inside IDE, let me know.

Reproduction cmd line looks like this:
```
./gradlew ':x-pack:plugin:sql:test' --tests "org.elasticsearch.xpack.sql.planner.QueryTranslatorSpecTests" -Dtests.method="test {querytranslator_tests.txt/NoCountDoesNotTrackHits}" -Dtests.seed=BF93038714D8F6B -Dtests.locale=en-IE -Dtests.timezone=Africa/Sao_Tome -Druntime.java=16
```

timeline.body: Do we have tests where the same query is ran against more than one matcher?

reply.body: yep sure, please check: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/71829/files#diff-ae8ba179d732e7ad13176e9c0645cc9b5a26b0c9300fe8edbadf22648e334507R138 for example.

timeline.body: Any reason why contains need to be specified? Since it's an either/or option - either there's nothing specified (contains) or something else such as regex - specifying contains is redundant.

reply.body:
I kept it, just because it could help when you have multiple assertions of mixed regex and simple contains and could make sense to have something like:
```
contains <match1>
regex <match2>
regex <match3>
contains <match4>
...
```
Since it doesn't complicate the code (it's only a couple of extra lines), I thought it would be nice to have it as an option. If you insist  though I can remove it and keep only the implicit version.

timeline.body:
Looks good overall - left some comments around some further simplifications.
Glad to see we're gaining ~400 lines back despite formatting.
Btw, I think we should include this in 7.13 as well - it's just testing so it doesn't affect shipped code however it will make backporting (if needed) easier.

+//
+// Query translator tests. Format:
+//
+// <name>[-Ignore]
+// <sql-query-line1>
+// [<sql-query-line2>
+// ...
+// <sql-query-line-n];
+// [<matcher-1> <expectation-1>EOL
+// <matcher-2> <expectation-2>EOL
+// ...
+// ]
+// ;
+//
+// Notes:
+//   - The SQL query could span multiple lines and should be terminated with semicolon (;)
+//   - The currently supported matchers: `CONTAINS` (the default one), `STARTS_WITH`, `ENDS_WITH`, `REGEX`
+//   - To ignore a test, add the -Ignore to the end of the name
+//   - Matchers can be skipped, if you just want to test that a query is optimized/plan without errors
+//   - Do not use whitespaces in the relevant parts of the query itself, as they will be removed.
+//     For example to match: '"params":{"v0":"point","v1":"point( 10 20 )"}
+//     you should use: "point(1020)" instead of "point( 10 20 )", otherwise the assertion will fail.
+
+// Subqueries
+/////////////
+SubqueryBasicSelect
+SELECT int FROM
+    (SELECT int FROM test);
+;
+
+SubquerySelectOnFieldAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test);
+;
+
+SubqueryGroupByNoAlias
+SELECT int FROM
+    (SELECT int FROM test)
+GROUP BY int;
+;
+
+SubqueryGroupByOnFieldAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test)
+GROUP BY i;
+;
+
+SubqueryFilterOrderByAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test)
+WHERE i IS NOT NULL
+ORDER BY i;
+;
+
+SubqueryGroupByFilterAndOrderByByAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test)
+WHERE i IS NOT NULL
+GROUP BY i
+ORDER BY i;
+;
+
+SubqueryFilterByAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test)
+WHERE i > 10;
+;
+
+SubqueryOrderByAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test)
+ORDER BY i;
+;
+
+SubqueryWithAliasBasicSelect
+SELECT int FROM
+    (SELECT int FROM test) AS s;
+;
+
+SubqueryWithAliasBasicQualifiedSelect
+SELECT s.int FROM
+    (SELECT int FROM test) AS s;
+;
+
+SubqueryWithAliasSelectOnFieldAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test) AS s;
+;
+
+SubqueryWithAliasQualifiedSelectOnFieldAlias
+SELECT s.i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test) AS s;
+;
+
+SubqueryWithAliasGroupBy
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test) AS s
+GROUP BY s.i;
+;
+
+SubqueryWithAliasFilterByAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test) AS s
+WHERE s.i > 10;
+;
+
+SubqueryWithAliasOrderByAlias
+SELECT i FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test) AS s
+ORDER BY s.i > 10;
+;
+
+MultiLevelSubqueriesOrderByByAlias1
+SELECT i AS j FROM
+    (SELECT int AS i FROM test)
+ORDER BY j;
+;
+
+MultiLevelSubqueriesOrderByByAlias2
+SELECT j AS k FROM
+    (SELECT i AS j FROM
+        (SELECT int AS i FROM test)
+    )
+ORDER BY k;
+;
+
+SubqueryGroupByOrderByAliasedExpression
+SELECT int_group AS g, min_date AS d FROM (
+   SELECT int % 2 AS int_group, MIN(date) AS min_date
+   FROM test WHERE date > '1970-01-01'::datetime
+   GROUP BY int_group
+)
+ORDER BY d DESC;
+;
+
+SubqueryGroupByOrderByAliasedAggFunction
+SELECT int_group AS g, min_date AS d FROM (
+    SELECT int % 2 AS int_group, MIN(date) AS min_date
+    FROM test WHERE date > '1970-01-01'::datetime
+    GROUP BY int_group
+)
+ORDER BY g DESC;
+;
+
+MultiLevelSubquerySelectStar
+SELECT * FROM (
+    SELECT * FROM (
+        SELECT * FROM test
+    )
+);
+;
+
+MultiLevelSubquerySelectStarWithAliases
+SELECT * FROM (
+    SELECT * FROM (
+        SELECT * FROM test
+    ) b
+) c;
+;
+
+MultiLevelSubqueryGroupBy1
+SELECT i AS j FROM (
+    SELECT int AS i FROM test
+)
+GROUP BY j;
+;
+
+MultiLevelSubqueryGroupBy2
+SELECT j AS k FROM (
+    SELECT i AS j FROM (
+        SELECT int AS i FROM test
+    )
+) GROUP BY k;
+;
+
+SubqueryGroupByFilterAndOrderByByRealiased
+SELECT g as h FROM (
+    SELECT date AS f, int AS g FROM test
+) WHERE h IS NOT NULL
+GROUP BY h
+ORDER BY h ASC;
+;
+
+FilterAfterGroupBy
+SELECT j AS k FROM (
+    SELECT i AS j FROM (
+        SELECT int AS i FROM test
+    )
+    GROUP BY j
+) WHERE j < 5;
+;
